newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian Sugar - Market quiet despite China rumours.
newsitem.headline: Asian Sugar - Market quiet despite China rumours.

text.p: Japan's physical sugar market has remained quiet in recent days, while traders mulled rumours, discounted by many, that China may be dipping into the market to buy.

Japanese traders said on Monday that premiums for Thai raw sugar were steady to slightly firmer after their recent easing, with March/May delivery, on a free-on-board (FOB) basis, quoted at 0.65/0.75 cent a lb (bid/offer) over the most-active March futures on New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE).
January/March delivery was quoted at 0.85/1.0 cent over New York futures while May/July was quoted at 0.65/0.75 cent over New York.
With Japanese sugar refiners likely to hold off on purchases until next year, traders said they were focusing on possible activity from China.
They noted vague rumours that emerged late last week of Chinese buying, which one trader said may have been price covering, although they had no details and several were sceptical of the talk.

"New York has come down quite a bit. There's a view that this is a level where Chinese buying would emerge, but they may be waiting for more declines," said one trader at a large Japanese trade house.

The most-active CSCE March 1997 futures slid about 10 percent in mid- to late-September, from a high of 11.76 cents a lb on September 11 to a 3-1/2-month-low of 10.60 cents a lb on September 27. Prices have since traded inside a 10.70 to 11.00 cent range.

Traders expected any Chinese buying to focus on the May/July or July/September 1997 delivery periods, with one saying the Chinese still appeared to be whittling down inventories after last year's heavy buying.
"They have enough to cover their needs through next March or April. They're working off inventories and there's nothing to light a fire under them," he said.
Traders added that sugar shipments to Japan from Australia and South Africa had been proceeding normally.
